The vertex set $V'$ of $G'$ is:
\[
V' = V'_1 \sqcup V'_2 \sqcup \ldots \sqcup V'_k, 
\]
where each $V_i'$ is a copy of $V$. 
We use $\vij{i}{j, \ell}_a$ for $a \in [k]$ to denote the copy of vertex $\vij{i}{j, \ell} \in V$ in set $V'_a$. 

The edge set of $G'$ will be composed of $(t \cdot r \cdot k)$-many $k$-cliques. 
For $i \in [t], j\in [r]$ and $\ell \in [k]$, we define the clique $\cliq{i, j, \ell}$ as the following set of edges. 
\[
	\cliq{i,j,\ell} = \{(\vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(a)}_{a}, \vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(b)}_b) \mid a, b \in [k] \textnormal{ with } a \neq b \}.
\]
This forms a $k$-clique between the following vertices:
\[
	\{ \vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(1)}_{1}, \vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(2)}_2, \ldots, \vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(k)}_k\}.
\]
The edge set $E'$ will be the union of all $\cliq{i,j, \ell}$ for $i \in [t], j \in[r]$ and $\ell \in [k]$.
It is easy to see that $G'$ is $k$-colorable. Each copy $V'_i$ can be colored with one color, as there are no edges between any two vertices in the same copy. 

Observe that for any $i \in[t]$ the vertices of $\cliq{i, j, \ell}$ are disjoint from each other for all $j \in [r]$ and $\ell \in [k]$. For two vertices $\vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(a)}_{a}$ and $\vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell'}(a)}_a$ in the same layer $V'_{a}$ with $\ell \neq \ell'$, the values of $\tau_{\ell}(a)$ and $\tau_{\ell'}(a)$ are distinct. 

We define the partition of $E'$ into $t$ sets as follows. For $i \in [t]$, 
\[
	E'_i = \bigcup_{j \in [r], \ell \in [k]} \cliq{i, j, \ell}.
\]
As we argued that cliques $\cliq{i,j, \ell}$ are disjoint for $j \in [r], \ell \in [k]$, we can see that $E'_i$ is a $k$-cluster of size $r \cdot k$. It remains to prove the inducedness condition required in cluster-packing graphs. 

Consider any two vertices $\vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(a)}_a$ and $\vij{i}{j', \tau_{\ell'}(b)}_b$ inside the subgraph induced by $E'_i$. Assume towards a contradiction that an edge exists between these two vertices, and it comes from some partition $E'_{\ensuremath{i^{\star}}}$ for $\ensuremath{i^{\star}} \in [t]$, with $\ensuremath{i^{\star}} \neq i$. 
Then, these vertices must be of the form:
\[
	\vij{i}{j, \tau_{\ell}(a)}_a = \vij{\ensuremath{i^{\star}}}{\ensuremath{j^{\star}}, \tau_{\ensuremath{\ell^{\star}}}(a)}_a \qquad  \vij{i}{j', \tau_{\ell'}(b)}_b = \vij{\ensuremath{i^{\star}}}{\ensuremath{j^{\star}}, \tau_{\ensuremath{\ell^{\star}}}(b)}_b,
\]
for some $\ensuremath{j^{\star}} \in [r], \ensuremath{\ell^{\star}} \in [k]$. 
By definition of $E'$, if an edge exists between these two vertices, an edge also exists between vertices $\vij{\ensuremath{i^{\star}}}{\ensuremath{j^{\star}}, \tau_{\ensuremath{\ell^{\star}}}(a)}$ and $\vij{\ensuremath{i^{\star}}}{\ensuremath{j^{\star}}, \tau_{\ensuremath{\ell^{\star}}}(b)}$ in the original graph $G$, from the partition $E_{\ensuremath{i^{\star}}}$. However, these vertices are present in the subgraph induced by partition $E_i$, and this violates the inducedness property of $E_i$, giving a contradiction.

    \end{align}

    $,

    \[
    t \leqslant \frac{1}{\varepsilon\cdot \delta} = O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon\cdot \delta}),
    \]
    concluding the proof.

\label{fact:it-facts}
  Let $\rv{A}$, $\rv{B}$, $\rv{C}$, and $\rv{D}$ be four (possibly correlated) random variables.
   \begin{enumerate}
  \item \label{part:uniform} $0 \leqslant \en{\rv{A}} \leqslant \log{\card{\supp{\rv{A}}}}$. The right equality holds
    iff $\distribution{\rv{A}}$ is uniform.
  \item \label{part:info-zero} $\mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}} \geqslant 0$. The equality holds iff $\rv{A}$ and
    $\rv{B}$ are \emph{independent} conditioned on $\rv{C}$.
    \item \label{part:info-entropy} $\mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}} \leqslant \en{\rv{B}}$ for any random variables $\rv{A}, \rv{B}, \rv{C}$. 
  \item \label{part:cond-reduce} \emph{Conditioning on a random variable reduces entropy}:
    $\en{\rv{A} \mid \rv{B},\rv{C}} \leqslant \en{\rv{A} \mid  \rv{B}}$.  The equality holds iff $\rv{A} \perp \rv{C} \mid \rv{B}$.



  \item \label{part:chain-rule} \emph{Chain rule for mutual information}: $\mi{\rv{A},\rv{B}}{\rv{C} \mid \rv{D}} = \mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{C} \mid \rv{D}} + \mi{\rv{B}}{\rv{C} \mid  \rv{A},\rv{D}}$.
  \item \label{part:data-processing} \emph{Data processing inequality}: for a function $f(\rv{A})$ of $\rv{A}$, $\mi{f(\rv{A})}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}} \leqslant \mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}}$. 
   \end{enumerate}

First, we prove the equality between the second term and the third term in the statement. 
\begin{align*}
	\tvd{\rv{X}\ensuremath{\rv{Z}}}{\rv{Y}\ensuremath{\rv{Z}}} &=\frac12 \cdot \sum_{W, Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[(W, Z)] \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X}\ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = (W, Z)] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y}\ensuremath{\rv{Z}}=(W, Z)]}  \\
	&=\frac12 \cdot \sum_{W, Z}  \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] \cdot (\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid  \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}}= Z])} \\
	&= \sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{Z}} =Z] \cdot \frac12 \sum_{W}  \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid  \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}}= Z]} \\
	&= \sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{Z}} =Z] \cdot\tvd{(\rv{X} \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}}= Z)}{(\rv{Y} \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z)} \\
	&= \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{Z} \tvd{(\rv{X} \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}}= Z)}{(\rv{Y} \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z)}.
\end{align*}

Now we prove the inequality between the first term and the third term. 
\begin{align*}
		\tvd{\rv{X}}{\rv{Y}} &= \frac12 \cdot \sum_{W} \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W]} \\
		&= \frac12 \cdot \sum_{W} \card{\sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z](\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z])} \\
		& \leqslant  \frac12 \cdot \sum_{W}  \sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z]} \\
		&= \sum_{Z}   \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] \cdot \paren{\frac12 \cdot \sum_{W} \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z]}}  \\
		&= \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{Z} \tvd{\rv{X} \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}}= Z}{\rv{Y} \mid \ensuremath{\rv{Z}} = Z}. \qedhere
\end{align*}
